content:
Prince Harry and Meghan Markle withdrew their two children from their school just two days into the academic year.

According to a report first published by Hello! magazine, 5-year-old Prince Archie and 3-year-old Princess Lili were taken out of school because the couple's security team raised safety concerns.

The report stated that Harry and Meghan's private security team had warned about potential risks facing the family, including heavy traffic near the school and long commutes. Hello! also reported an incident that made it difficult for the family's motorcade to travel together.

A spokesperson for the Sussex couple told HuffPost: "The decision to change the children's school was made after discussing with the family's security team whether the current arrangements were workable."

The spokesperson added: "The parents are deeply grateful for all the love and care that the school's teachers and staff have consistently shown their family. This decision absolutely does not reflect any negative view of the school, nor any suggestion that the school has fallen short in caring for the children."

Since Harry stepped down from royal duties, he lost his government-funded police protection and has since expressed concerns about security arrangements in the UK.

He launched a legal challenge against this decision, claiming the current arrangements put him and his family at extreme risk.

Speaking to the BBC in May 2025, with the family in the United States at the time, Harry said: "I cannot see any possibility of bringing my wife and children back to the UK at this stage."

Since they are currently in the UK, the Royal and Executive Committee for the Protection of Royal and VIPs (RAVEC) will conduct a fresh official risk assessment for the couple, according to the Daily Telegraph.
